label_policy.origin: Provisional fixture-author judgments. The corpus and questions are synthetic and authored together; no independent human relevance review has been performed.
label_policy.languages: English (en), Spanish (es), and Hungarian (hu) query wording is provisional author wording, not independently validated by native speakers. Every indexed source is in English.
label_policy.unit: Judgments apply to complete source documents identified by paths relative to corpus/. A retrieved chunk inherits its source grade; this can over-credit a chunk that omits the relevant passage.

grade_definitions.0: Does not support the requested answer; includes misleading same-keyword matches about a different mechanism.
grade_definitions.1: Related context or terminology, but insufficient evidence for a requested answer or a substantial answer facet.
grade_definitions.2: Useful partial evidence for the requested answer, but incomplete for the facet it addresses.
grade_definitions.3: Directly answers the request or directly supplies a distinct required facet of a multi-source request.

label_policy.completeness: Every query explicitly judges every source, including zero-grade distractors. Missing judgments must not be inferred as zero.
label_policy.multi_source: For q03, both docs/representation-identity.md and docs/collection-handoff.md are required for complete source coverage. Retrieving multiple chunks from one source cannot cover the other source.
label_policy.heldout_boundary: Only corpus/docs/*.md may be ingested. This query manifest, grades, titles, tags, rationales, and evaluation outputs remain outside the indexed corpus. The fixed split is for evaluation, not a claim of independent corpus design or representative production quality.
label_policy.measurement: Grade 2 or 3 means relevant for binary recall and reciprocal-rank metrics. Graded ranking metrics retain the full 0-3 scale. No model performance is asserted by the fixture itself.

queries.title: Keep searches available during replacement
queries.text: People must keep finding documents while we prepare a replacement collection. What ordering lets ongoing requests finish safely and makes fresh requests use the completed replacement?

judgments.rationale: Directly gives staging, validation, atomic publication, request pinning, and delayed reclamation.
Explains why interrupted staging cannot replace published data, but omits reader pinning and the successful handoff.
Controls the timing of source refreshes rather than collection publication or concurrent readers.
Describes removing and adding source paths, not keeping a collection available during replacement.
Describes text segmentation and contains no publication sequence.
Describes result limits rather than which collection a request reads.
Requires compatible manifests before serving, but delegates the publication procedure and says nothing about reader lifetimes.
Provides atomic visibility for one document revision, which is narrower than a whole-collection reader handoff.
Describes language matching, not availability during collection replacement.
Describes encoder input sizing, not reader availability.
Describes transport failure retries and no publication sequence.
Discusses collection snapshots, but its restore procedure stops readers and cannot supply the requested online handoff.
Batches notifications after source updates, without controlling which collection serves requests.
Formats retrieved passages and does not manage collection generations.

queries.title: Combine editor event bursts before refresh
queries.text: Which batching rule should combine repeated file changes before the search index is refreshed, so a burst of editor saves reads each final file state once without postponing work forever?

judgments.rationale: Controls collection publication, not coalescing repeated file events.
Reuses work after an interrupted build and supplies no event-batching policy.

Explains absent-path cleanup during moves, but does not explain coalescing saves or bounded waiting.
Groups text into passages rather than watcher events into work.
Limits returned matches, not pending file work.
Defines encoder compatibility and contains no watcher scheduling policy.
Explains the update transaction after passages are prepared, but not how events are batched before that update.
Discusses multilingual matching and no file-event policy.
Batches encoder inputs by capacity; it cannot choose a final file state or bound watcher-event delay.
Waits between failed transport attempts rather than coalescing successful editor events.
Schedules saved snapshots rather than processing edit bursts.
Hard same-keyword distractor: file changes batching and quiet/max timers delay email notices after refresh, not index refresh work.
Controls the presentation of existing matches and no refresh scheduling.

queries.title: Replace an encoder while preserving service
queries.text: We are switching to another embedding encoder. Which stored representation settings define what must be rebuilt, and how should the finished replacement take over while existing searches continue?

judgments.rationale: Directly supplies the required availability facet: build separately, validate, publish atomically, and retain pinned readers.
Explains preserving published data on replacement failure and manifest-aware reuse, but omits the complete compatibility identity and successful reader handoff.
Combines file events and does not define representation compatibility or a collection handoff.
Changes source ownership paths rather than encoder representation identity.
Describes segmentation, without naming compatibility identity fields or publication behavior.
Sets result counts after retrieval and does not address encoder migration.
Directly supplies the required identity facet: encoder, revision, width, both roles, normalization, a fresh namespace, and corpus re-encoding.
Explains an atomic replacement of one source revision, but not a corpus-wide representation change or concurrent collection readers.
Mentions a shared compatible encoder and separate roles, but does not enumerate identity fields or the migration sequence.
Mentions document-role tokens during preparation, but omits representation identity and publication.
Rejects incompatible vector widths, but does not define the other identity fields or a migration.
Restores a saved collection with readers stopped; it cannot provide the requested encoder migration with ongoing searches.
Changes notification timing rather than representations or collection readers.
Formats returned matches and does not manage stored representations.

queries.title: Remove old passages after a shorter edit
queries.text: An edited document is much shorter, but searches still find sentences we deleted. What must the successful update replace or remove so readers cannot get a mixture of its old and new versions?

judgments.rationale: Discusses generation isolation for whole collections, but does not explain deleting surplus passages owned by one source.
Checks completed staging entries after failure, but does not prescribe replacement of all passage rows for an edited source.
Reads a final changed file state once; it does not specify removal of surplus rows when the file becomes shorter.
Purges rows for a vanished old path, but this question concerns an edit under the same owner.
Defines passage construction and ownership, but not transactional removal of obsolete revisions.
Filtering or limiting matches does not remove obsolete stored passages.
Deals with encoder compatibility rather than editing a document under the same representation.
Directly requires replacing the complete owner row set in one transaction, deleting surplus old rows, and exposing one revision at a time.
Changes language matching behavior, not stored source revisions.
Prevents overlong encoder inputs and does not delete old passage rows.
Retries temporary transport failures rather than replacing stale source revisions.
An offline snapshot restore can reintroduce older content and does not specify the successful source update.
Deleting a notice does not remove indexed passages and cannot repair stale text.
Distinguishes formatting from stored revisions, but supplies no update transaction or deletion rule.

queries.title: Eliminar la copia anterior tras mover una guía
queries.text: Moví una guía a otra carpeta y ahora aparecen tanto la ubicación anterior como la nueva al buscar. ¿Cómo se debe representar ese cambio para que desaparezca la copia antigua?

judgments.rationale: Publishes collections, but does not define path identity or move cleanup.
Handles interrupted staging work, not a source changing locations.
Explains that a finally absent path removes its indexed passages, providing useful cleanup evidence but not the full two-owner move rule.
Directly defines a move as removing the old path owner and ingesting the destination, with inventory reconciliation for lingering copies.
Preserves passage ownership and locations, but does not describe changing owners after a move.
Result duplicate filtering does not repair the obsolete source owner.
Defines encoder identity, not source path identity.
Explains purging and replacing all rows owned by a source, useful for cleanup, but distinguishes that operation from moving to a new path.
Spanish-language input is incidental; the requested operation is path cleanup, not cross-language matching.

Describes transport errors, not relocation bookkeeping.
Describes restoring snapshots rather than reconciling moved source paths.
Notification deletion does not delete source data or repair duplicate locations.
Displays a source link but cannot delete the data that makes the old location searchable.

queries.title: Conservar el sentido de tablas y secciones
queries.text: Al dividir un manual largo para buscar fragmentos, ¿cómo evitamos que una fila pierda los nombres de sus columnas o que un párrafo quede separado del título que le da contexto?

judgments.rationale: Controls collection readers, not textual context across passage boundaries.
Describes resuming a build and no table or heading segmentation.
Groups filesystem events, not rows or paragraphs.
Tracks owning paths rather than context within a document.

Limits returned matches and does not preserve the meaning of stored fragments.
Defines vector compatibility fields and no document-structure rules.
Stores complete passage sets with ownership, but does not define section or table boundaries.
The query language is incidental; language-space compatibility does not preserve headings during segmentation.
Requires oversized text to be divided at suitable boundaries while retaining provenance, but does not specify table or section heading retention.
Rejects invalid transport inputs and does not explain how to retain textual context.

Groups change notices into email, not document text into meaningful passages.
Shows section titles and excerpts after retrieval, but does not preserve headings when creating stored passages.

queries.title: Consultar fuentes inglesas desde otro idioma
queries.text: La documentación está en inglés, pero el equipo pregunta en español o en húngaro. ¿Qué permite recuperar una respuesta pertinente sin exigir palabras idénticas ni traducir antes todos los documentos?

judgments.rationale: Describes collection publication, not matching meaning across languages.
Verifies interrupted build work, not language compatibility.
Controls event timing and does not address multilingual questions.
Tracks moved source paths, not language matching.

Provides compatible query/document roles and the shared representation checks needed for retrieval, but does not establish multilingual capability.

Retries failed requests and provides no language-space mechanism.

queries.title: Miért érkezik kevesebb találat?
queries.text: Húsz találatot kértem, mégis csak hetet kaptam. Milyen korlátok miatt lehet ez szabályos működés, és mely számokból derül ki, hogy a kérés felső határa vagy a megfelelő találatok hiánya okozta?

judgments.rationale: Selects a complete collection and does not define result-count diagnostics.

Bounds file-event delay rather than the number of search results.

queries.title: Helyreállás félbeszakadt felépítés után
queries.text: Az új gyűjtemény építése közben elfogyott a tárhely. Újraindításkor miből szolgáljuk ki a kereséseket, és hogyan döntjük el, hogy a félkész munka mely részei használhatók fel újra?

queries.title: Túl hosszú bemenet az enkóder számára
queries.text: Egyetlen szövegrész sem fér bele az enkóder bemeneti keretébe, hiába küldök egyszerre kevesebb elemet. Hogyan készítsük elő a szöveget úgy, hogy a vége se vesszen el, és az eredeti forrás továbbra is azonosítható legyen?
